indication: Refractory Viral Keratitis/Herpes Simplex Virus Infection

endpoints.name: HSV-1 testing results
endpoints.definition: HSV-1 testing results of the intervention eye. Tear swab of 1 week, 1 month, 2 months, 3 months, 6 months and 12 months post-operation will be collected and quantified for HSV-1 genome by real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). The virus testing outcome was indicated as positive (+) or negative (-) by Ct values. Ct value of above 40 will be considered negative, 36-40 be considered weakly positive, and below 35 will be considered a strong positive.

ELISA and Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) will be conducted on the blood samples collected at 3-month and 6-month visit, respectively.

interim_analysis.details: Part B uses adaptive Bayesian methodology. For anti-PD-(L)1 naive patients (B3, B4): predictive probability calculated after 12 patients to assess chance of observing ≥8 of 35 responses. Interim analysis at 20 patients if predictive probability ≥20%. Arms stopped if predictive probability <20%. For anti-PD-(L)1 pretreated patients (B1, B2): predictive probability for ≥3 of 20 responses after 10 patients, no formal interim analysis. Arm B8 incorporates futility monitoring beginning with 15th patient for chance of 13 responses in 48 patients.

sample_size.n: Part A: ~30 evaluable patients per treatment arm for dose-escalation, ~18 for safety run-in, ~20 per tumor type for solid malignancy cohorts. Part B: 10-55 patients for B1-B6 depending on arm, 48 patients each for B7-B8
sample_size.power: Not specified for efficacy. Operating characteristics: Part A CRM selects correct dose 50.9-60.1% of trials
sample_size.assumptions: Part B: 9% probability of <12 responses given 35% true response rate for B7; 20% probability given 25% true response rate for B8

sensitivity_analyses.name: Missing data sensitivity analysis

sensitivity_analyses.name: Tipping point analysis
sensitivity_analyses.applied_to: Exploring extent of departures from assumptions
sensitivity_analyses.details: Characterised as extent of departures from assumptions that change interpretation of results in terms of statistical or clinical significance

methods.name: Group sequential designs
methods.details: Used to facilitate the conduct of interim analysis, most commonly applied because it is more practicable to assess grouped subject outcomes at periodic intervals during the trial than on a continuous basis

methods.name: Meta-analysis
methods.details: Formal evaluation of quantitative evidence from two or more trials bearing on the same question, involving statistical combination of summary statistics

methods.name: Intention-to-treat analysis
methods.details: Primary analysis should include all randomised subjects following intention-to-treat principle

methods.name: Per protocol analysis
methods.details: Analysis of subjects who complied with protocol sufficiently, usually conducted alongside full analysis set

methods.name: Confidence intervals
methods.details: Estimates of treatment effects should be accompanied by confidence intervals whenever possible

methods.name: Survival analysis methods
methods.details: Should be considered when substantial proportion of treatment withdrawals or deaths are expected to calculate cumulative adverse event rates

multiplicity.details: When multiplicity is present from multiple primary variables, multiple comparisons of treatments, repeated evaluation over time and/or interim analyses, adjustment to type I error may be necessary. Methods to avoid or reduce multiplicity are preferable when available
multiplicity.alpha_allocation: Conventionally type I error set at 5% or less or as dictated by multiplicity considerations

interim_analysis.spending_function: Flexible alpha spending function approaches may be employed
interim_analysis.details: Should be carefully planned in advance and described in protocol. Statistical methods should be fully specified in advance. Goal is to stop trial early if superiority clearly established, if demonstration of relevant treatment difference has become unlikely, or if unacceptable adverse effects are apparent

sample_size.power: Type II error conventionally set at 10% to 20%
sample_size.assumptions: Should specify primary variable, test statistic, null hypothesis, alternative hypothesis, type I error (conventionally 5% or less), type II error (10-20%), and approach to dealing with treatment withdrawals and protocol violations

interim_analysis.details: Interim futility analyses based on proportion of clinical progression by cycle 1. Data Monitoring Committee will review all cases where progressive disease is confirmed or suspected. If progression convincingly exceeds 10%, accrual will be suspended. Early stopping rules with posterior probability of progression >10% being 75% or higher will trigger enrollment hold.

sample_size.assumptions: Projected pCR rate of 25% (20 responders and 60 non-responders), to detect AUC significantly greater than 0.65 vs null of AUC ≤0.65, true AUC of 0.80, one-sided type I error rate of 0.10. Maximum overall accrual of 88 patients accounting for 10% major protocol violations/missing data.

sensitivity_analyses.description: OCR rate conducted in the FAS

sensitivity_analyses.name: RFS sensitivity analysis
sensitivity_analyses.description: RFS conducted in the FAS, and sensitivity analyses similar to DOR

indication: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma (diffuse large B cell lymphoma or aggressive B-cell lymphoma) post autologous hematopoietic stem cell transplant
design: Multi-center dose escalation study with two components

endpoints.name: Component 1: Establish MTD of FT596 at Day 30 post-transplant
endpoints.definition: Maximum tolerated dose when given 30 days after transplant

endpoints.name: Component 2: Confirm MTD and safety of FT596 at Day 7 post-transplant
endpoints.definition: Confirm the MTD and safety of giving a single dose of FT596 at Day 7 post-transplant using one dose level below the MTD (MTD -1) or the MTD from Component 1

endpoints.name: Adverse events related to FT596 and rituximab
endpoints.definition: Evaluate adverse events related to FT596 administered post auto-HSCT in combination with rituximab

endpoints.name: Progression free survival (PFS) and relapse/progression at 12 months
endpoints.definition: Determine preliminary efficacy based on progression free survival (PFS) and relapse/progression at 12 months post auto-HSCT

endpoints.name: Non-relapse mortality
endpoints.definition: Determine the incidence of non-relapse mortality at 100 days and 1 year post auto-HSCT

endpoints.name: FT596 persistence
endpoints.definition: Evaluate persistence of FT596 in blood after each FT596 infusion by immunophenotyping and PCR up to 1 year

endpoints.name: Association of FT596 persistence with safety and activity
endpoints.definition: Assess the association of FT596 cell persistence with safety and anti-tumor activity

endpoints.name: Association of baseline characteristics with response
endpoints.definition: Assess the association of baseline clinical and tumor characteristics with safety and response endpoints following administration of FT596

methods.name: Modified Continual Reassessment Method (CRM)
methods.details: Power model for probability of DLT, target toxicity rate ≤25%, uses Bayesian framework

methods.name: Immunophenotyping
methods.details: Flow cytometry analysis of PBMC to detect surface markers and intracellular markers

methods.name: PCR testing
methods.details: PCR testing for FT596 persistence up to 1 year

sample_size.assumptions: Low expected toxicity, most likely 12 patients per component

populations.name: Intention-to-treat (ITT)
populations.definition: All patients who receive at least one dose of FT596

indication: Cancer immunotherapy trials

endpoints.name: iCR (immune complete response)
endpoints.definition: Complete response using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

endpoints.name: iPR (immune partial response)
endpoints.definition: Partial response using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

endpoints.name: iSD (immune stable disease)
endpoints.definition: Stable disease using iRECIST criteria - may occur after prior iUPD

endpoints.name: iUPD (immune unconfirmed progression)
endpoints.definition: Initial progression by RECIST 1.1 criteria requiring confirmation

endpoints.name: iCPD (immune confirmed progression)
endpoints.definition: Confirmed progression after iUPD showing further increase or new lesions

endpoints.name: iPFS (immune progression-free survival)
endpoints.definition: Time from treatment start to confirmed progression (iCPD) or death

methods.name: iRECIST criteria
methods.details: Modified RECIST 1.1 allowing for pseudoprogression patterns, requires confirmation of initial progression

methods.name: RECIST 1.1
methods.details: Standard response criteria - recommended to continue as primary for randomized licensing trials

censoring_rules.event: First date of iUPD if subsequently confirmed as iCPD, or death
censoring_rules.censoring: Censor if iUPD not confirmed and patient has subsequent iSD, iPR or iCR; censor if patient stops treatment due to clinical instability or no further assessments done

populations.name: Clinically stable patients
populations.definition: Patients with no worsening performance status, no clinically relevant increase in disease symptoms, no requirement for intensified symptom management after iUPD

sensitivity_analyses.name: RECIST 1.1 vs iRECIST comparison
sensitivity_analyses.details: Recommended to collect both RECIST 1.1 and iRECIST data to compare outcomes and validate iRECIST

sensitivity_analyses.name: Independent imaging review
sensitivity_analyses.details: Central collection of scans recommended for all trials, independent review when feasible
